C's tnt.c (b->by_player) and serverreplay.c's End TNT blast (end_blast_igniter) passed SURV_EXPLOSION, which survival.c always scaled. On the Java client the player's own TNT took 17 hp at easy, 17 at hard and 18 at peaceful (unscaled); C took 9.5, a death and 0. Fixed in survival.c: SURV_EXPLOSION is scaled unless its attacker is the player. At normal the scaling is the identity, so no normal row moves

cause: Read against oracle/src, no recording: EntityZombie.func_146070_a adds the door-breaking task only when the flag changes, so a zombie whose onSpawnWithEgg passes both the door roll (nextFloat < f*0.1) and the leader roll (the max-health bonus, which sets the flag again) has the task once. C's hostiles.c (the direct onSpawnWithEgg path: spawner blocks and dev summons) calls ai_add_break_door at both rolls, and add_task_full does not deduplicate: two tasks, two nextInt(20) draws a tick at a door. The natural spawner path (serverreplay.c) guards it. About 0.5% of zombies at normal (f up to 1), more at hard. lane/divaudit: the reach is narrower than read. Dev summons and villager infection take serverreplay_summon_hostile's record path, which runs the egg at local difficulty 0 and sets the task once from the record (break_doors || leader); 8,000 dev summons at hard and full moon replayed equal. Only a mob-spawner block's zombie (serverreplay.c's tile spawner, living_on_spawn_with_egg_ret at the real local difficulty) reaches hostiles.c's double add. The guard (add only when the flag changes) is in d62db462, unpinned: no dev op makes a zombie spawner (setblock gives TileEntityMobSpawner's default Pig) or raises inhabitedTime, and at hard with no inhabited time both rolls pass for about 3 zombies in 10,000
repro: a zombie spawner's zombies at night, local difficulty high, at a wooden door (needs a dev op for a spawner's EntityId or a chunk's inhabitedTime)

cause: Read against oracle/src, no recording: EntitySkeleton.attackEntityWithRangedAttack's Power bonus is setDamage(getDamage() + (double)var4 * 0.5D + 0.5D), evaluated ((d + p*0.5) + 0.5); C's hostiles_skeleton.c adds (p*0.5 + 0.5) to d, which can differ by one ulp of the arrow's damage. Any difficulty; only a skeleton whose bow rolled Power. lane/divaudit: the two orders differ only by double rounding, which needs d two binades finer than d + p * 0.5 before the + 0.5 crosses a binade: Power III with d under 0.5 (close range, easy) is the common case; Power I needs d under 0.25; II, IV and V leave at most one extra bit and round alike (read, not measured). Recorded: 40 arrows from a Power III bow at easy, two blocks off; master's d.ents first differs at row 419. Fixed in hostiles_skeleton.c (dmg = dmg + p * 0.5 + 0.5)
